scope_changes: Implemented relationship repointing for compact/refine merge losers so relationships incident to canonical entities remain connected when the other endpoint is removed.
Added a dedicated approved canonical entity update/archive method and MCP tool; ordinary update_memory remains unchanged.

Pair-loop iteration 1: normalized stray tab characters to spaces inside two SQL string literals in postgres.py (decay_unused_priorities RETURNING clause and _apply_recall_decay UPDATE f-string); no SQL semantics changed.

Pair-loop iteration 1: extended materialize_archive canonical-entity mutation-site guard so the automated run_lifecycle_pipeline path skips canonical entities (defense-in-depth) using the shared is_canonical_entity helper; added a regression test.

Codex adversarial fix: approved_update_canonical_entity now captures the audit trail from the ORIGINAL pre-merge server metadata and always sets metadata['audit'] from that append-only list after merging params.metadata, so a caller-supplied 'audit' key can no longer erase prior audit history (AC3).

Codex adversarial fix: added shared async helper _filter_out_newly_canonical(conn, ids) reusing canonical_entity_protection_predicate() and called it immediately before the relationship-repoint/usage-log/DELETE steps in compact_memories and in the refine 'merge' case, narrowing the TOCTOU window in which a candidate promoted to a protected canonical entity after planning could still have its relationships repointed and usage logs deleted. Filtered ids are counted (protected_canonical_entities in compact, protected_skipped in refine); the already-guarded final DELETE remains the last line of defense (AC2).
downstream_impacts: DataLayer implementations must now provide approved_update_canonical_entity.
DecayResult, CompactResult, and RefineResult include protected_canonical_entities counts.
Supported read payloads may now include a canonical_entity object with id and kind.
